title: Fritaja sa šparogama (Istrian asparagus omelette)

ingredients.name: wild or thin green asparagus, tough ends removed
small onion or 2 spring onions, finely chopped

steps: Cut the asparagus into 2 cm pieces, keeping the tips separate, and blanch the stalks in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain well.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan, cook the onion for 3 minutes, then add the garlic and the asparagus pieces and sauté for another 4 to 5 minutes until just tender.
Beat the eggs with salt, pepper and the cheese, if using.
Pour the eggs over the asparagus and stir gently for a minute, then leave to set over low heat for about 5 minutes, without stirring, until the bottom is golden.
Slide the fritaja onto a plate, flip it back into the pan and cook the second side for 2 minutes, or finish it under a grill until set.
Serve warm or at room temperature in wedges, with bread and a green salad.

title: Fuži s piletinom (Istrian fuži pasta with chicken sauce)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
chopped parsley and grated hard cheese to serve

steps: Mix the flour, eggs, oil and salt in a bowl, adding warm water a spoonful at a time, then knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth, firm dough. Wrap it and rest for 30 minutes.
Season the chicken and brown it in 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a wide pan. Remove it, then soften the onion in the same pan for about 6 minutes and add the garlic.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the wine and let it reduce by half. Return the chicken, add the stock, cover and simmer for 40 minutes until the meat is falling off the bone.
Take the chicken out, shred the meat, discard the bones and return the meat to the sauce, simmering a few more minutes to thicken.

Roll the dough out about 2 mm thick, cut it into strips about 3 to 4 cm wide, then cut those diagonally into diamonds. Fold the two opposite points of each diamond over each other and pinch them together to make a small bow.
Cook the fuži in plenty of boiling salted water for about 4 to 5 minutes, until they float and are tender, then drain, reserving a little of the water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, loosening it with the reserved water if needed, and serve with parsley and grated cheese.

title: Gregada (Hvar island white fish and potato stew)

ingredients.name: firm white fish fillets or steaks (such as sea bass, hake, monkfish or grouper)
waxy potatoes, peeled and thickly sliced

steps: Layer the sliced onions and then the potatoes in the bottom of a wide, heavy pot. Season each layer lightly with salt and pepper.
Place the fish on top and scatter over the garlic and most of the parsley.
Pour over the olive oil, white wine and vinegar, then add just enough water to come level with the top of the potatoes, but not cover the fish entirely.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the fish is cooked through.
Do not stir with a spoon, as this breaks up the fish; instead shake the pot gently now and then to move the juices around.
Let the stew rest for 10 minutes off the heat, scatter with the remaining parsley and serve straight from the pot with crusty bread.

title: Istrian maneštra (bean, corn and potato soup)

ingredients.name: dried borlotti or cannellini beans, soaked overnight
sweetcorn kernels (fresh, or frozen and thawed)

steps: Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh water and simmer for about 45 minutes, until they are half-cooked.
In a large pot, heat the olive oil and fry the pancetta until it releases its fat. Add the onion and carrot and cook for about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, then add the beans with their cooking water, topping up with hot water to cover generously.
Add the potatoes and simmer for about 20 minutes, until the beans and potatoes are almost tender.
Stir in the corn and cook for another 10 minutes. Mash some of the beans and potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Season with salt and plenty of pepper, stir in the parsley and serve hot, with a drizzle of olive oil and bread.

title: Kotlovina (Zagreb-style fried pork and sausage stew)

ingredients.name: pork neck or loin chops, cut into large chunks
smoked or fresh pork sausages, sliced

steps: Season the pork chunks with salt and pepper. Heat the fat in a wide, heavy pan and brown the pork in batches until well coloured, then set aside.
Fry the sausage slices in the same fat until they have rendered some of their own fat and picked up colour.
Add the onions to the pan and cook for about 8 minutes, until soft and golden, then stir in the garlic and paprika for 30 seconds.
Return the meat to the pan, add the bell pepper and bay leaves and pour in the wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan and let the wine bubble for a minute.
Cover and cook over low heat for about 40 minutes, adding a splash of water only if it gets too dry; the meat should stew in its own juices.
Meanwhile fry or roast the potato wedges until crisp, and serve them with the kotlovina, bread and a salad of fresh cabbage or tomatoes.

title: Međimurska gibanica (Međimurje four-filling layer cake)

ingredients.name: ground walnuts, mixed with 50 g sugar
ground poppy seeds, mixed with 50 g sugar
apples, peeled and grated, mixed with 50 g sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan) and butter a large baking tin about 24 by 34 cm.
Mix the quark with the eggs, 100 g sugar, half of the sour cream and the vanilla until smooth. Keep the walnut, poppy seed and apple fillings in separate bowls.
Lay 3 sheets of filo in the tin, brushing each with melted butter, and spread over half of the walnut filling.
Add 2 buttered sheets and spread the poppy seed mixture, then 2 more and the apple filling.
Cover with 2 more sheets and the remaining walnuts, then finish with the cheese filling and the last 3 sheets, brushing each with butter.
Beat the remaining sour cream with a little melted butter and pour over the top. Bake for about 45 minutes until deep golden.
Cool a little, cut into squares and dust with icing sugar before serving.

title: Paprenjaci (Croatian honey and pepper biscuits)
steps: Warm the honey and sugar together gently until the sugar dissolves, then let the mixture cool until it is just lukewarm.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, walnuts, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg and baking soda.
Add the butter, egg and cooled honey mixture and knead to a smooth, slightly stiff dough. Wrap and chill for at least an hour.
Heat the oven to 170 C (150 C fan). Roll the dough to about 7 mm thick and cut it into rounds or squares, or press it into a floured wooden mould for the traditional pattern.
Place the biscuits on lined trays and bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until lightly browned and firm at the edges.
Cool on a rack. They are best after a day or two, once the pepper and spices have mellowed.

title: Pašticada (Dalmatian braised beef in sweet and sour sauce)

ingredients.name: beef round or topside, in one piece
smoked bacon or pancetta, cut into strips
sweet dessert wine (prošek, or sweet red/Marsala)

steps: With a thin knife, cut deep slits in the beef and push in the bacon strips, garlic halves, carrot sticks and cloves. Rub the meat with salt and pepper.
Put the meat in a bowl, pour over the vinegar and leave it covered in the fridge overnight, turning once.
Lift the beef out, pat it dry and brown it on all sides in the olive oil in a heavy casserole. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, soften the onions and celery for about 10 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, then stir in the tomato paste.
Return the beef, add the red wine, sweet wine, prunes, bay leaves, nutmeg and enough water to come about halfway up the meat.
Cover and cook very gently, on the hob or at 160 C in the oven, for about 3 hours, turning the meat occasionally, until it is very tender.
Lift out the beef and rest it. Press the sauce through a sieve, or blend it, and simmer it until thick and glossy.
Slice the beef thickly, return it to the sauce for a few minutes and serve with gnocchi or homemade pasta.

title: Pinca (Croatian Easter sweet bread)
steps: Stir the yeast and a spoonful of the sugar into the warm milk and leave for 10 minutes until foamy.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, the rest of the sugar, the salt and the zests, then add the foamy yeast, 4 eggs, the rum and the soft butter.
Knead for about 10 minutes, until the dough is soft, elastic and slightly sticky, then let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours.
Shape the dough into a round loaf, place it on a lined tray and cut a deep cross in the top with a sharp knife or scissors.
Let it rise again for about 45 minutes. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan).
Brush the loaf with beaten egg and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until a deep golden brown. Cool on a rack and serve in slices, traditionally at Easter.

title: Povitica (Croatian walnut roll)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, 75 g sugar and salt, then stir in the lukewarm milk, melted butter and egg yolks. Knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then let it rise, covered, for about an hour until doubled.
For the filling, mix the walnuts, 120 g sugar, cinnamon and cocoa, pour over the hot milk and add the butter. Stir until it forms a thick, spreadable paste, then cool.
Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan). Roll the dough out on a floured cloth, then stretch it with your hands until it is very thin, about 60 by 80 cm.
Spread the filling evenly over the dough, then use the cloth to help roll it up tightly from the long side into a long rope.
Coil the rope or fold it into a loaf shape inside a greased loaf tin, with the seam underneath, and let it rise again for 30 minutes.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, covering with foil if it browns too fast. Cool in the tin, then slice to show the spiral.

title: Rapska torta (Rab almond and maraschino cake)
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, then mix in the sugar, egg, liqueur and water to make a firm dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 130 C (110 C fan), a low temperature so that the almond filling cooks slowly without browning too much.
Mix the ground almonds, sugar, eggs, liqueur and the orange and lemon zest into a thick, moist paste.
Roll the dough out very thin and cut it into a wide strip and several long, narrow strips about 2 cm wide.
Lay the wide base of dough on baking paper, shape it into a round, and spread the almond filling over it.
Twist and wrinkle the narrow strips and wind them in a spiral over and around the filling, to give the cake its traditional ridged look.
Bake for 40 to 50 minutes, until the pastry is pale golden and the filling is set. Cool and dust generously with icing sugar before slicing.

title: Slavonski čobanac (Slavonian shepherd's meat stew)

ingredients.name: mixed meat: beef, pork and, if you can find it, game or lamb, cut into large cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot and fry the onions over medium heat for about 10 minutes, until soft and golden but not browned.
Add the meat and let it sear for about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it has lost its raw colour.
Take the pot off the heat for a moment, stir in the sweet and hot paprika so it does not burn, then return it to the heat.
Add the carrots, parsley root, garlic, salt and pepper, and pour in the water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, until the meat is meltingly tender and the broth is rich and red.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Serve in deep bowls with plenty of bread, or with noodles or potatoes.

title: Soparnik (Poljica Swiss chard pie)

ingredients.name: olive oil, plus more for the filling and brushing
Swiss chard or spinach, washed and finely chopped

steps: Knead the flour, warm water, 3 tablespoons of oil and the salt into a smooth, elastic dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 230 C (210 C fan), with a heavy baking tray inside to preheat.
Mix the chard with the onions, parsley, 3 tablespoons of oil and a good pinch of salt, squeezing and tossing until the chard begins to soften.
Divide the dough in two and roll each half into a very thin round, about 30 cm across.
Lay one round on a sheet of baking paper, pile the chard filling on top and spread it evenly, leaving a 2 cm rim. Cover with the second round, press the edges together and roll or crimp to seal.
Prick the top in a few places, slide the pie on its paper onto the hot tray and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the pastry is blistered and brown in places.
Mix the garlic with a little olive oil, brush it over the hot pie, cut it into wedges and serve warm.

title: Zagorski štrukli (baked Zagorje cheese pastry rolls)
steps: Knead the flour, one egg, oil, water and 1/2 teaspoon of salt into a soft, smooth dough. Cover it with a warm bowl and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan). Stir together the cottage cheese, 100 g of the sour cream, the two eggs and the salt for the filling.
Roll out the dough on a floured cloth, then stretch it with your hands until it is paper-thin and large enough to cover the table.
Brush the dough with some melted butter, spread the cheese filling in an even layer, and use the cloth to roll it up into a long roll.
Cut the roll into pieces about 6 cm long and set them upright, tightly packed, in a buttered baking dish.
Whisk the remaining sour cream with the milk and the last egg, pour it over the rolls, and drizzle with the rest of the butter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden on top and set. Serve warm as a main dish or a side.

title: Zlevanka (Međimurje sweet cornmeal and cottage cheese bake)

ingredients.name: jam or icing sugar to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan) and oil a large, shallow baking tray or dish.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the sour cream, oil, milk and vanilla, then add the cottage cheese and mix gently, leaving some small curds.
Mix the cornmeal, flour and baking powder and fold them in until just combined; the batter should be quite loose and pourable.
Pour the batter into the tray, which gives the dish its name, and spread it evenly.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and set. Cut into squares and serve warm with jam or dusted with icing sugar.
